section_0_paper_identification.paper_title: Tabular Placement of Relational Data on MEMS-based Storage Devices

section_1_goal_and_primary_metric.goal: To develop a data placement scheme for relational data on MEMS-based storage that exploits its two-dimensional physical characteristics to enable efficient retrieval in both row-wise and column-wise manners, thereby improving I/O utilization and cache performance.

concrete_numbers.meaning: Total I/O time for a full table scan of a 1.28M record relation with a 1-attribute projection, comparing NSM/PAX baseline to FRM.
Memory space saving for FRM compared to NSM/PAX when a query involves one of sixteen attributes.
FRM and PAX perform about three times better (fewer cache misses) than NSM on a selection query involving one attribute.

section_2_comparison_baseline.baseline_name: Disk-like mapping of MEMS storage with NSM/PAX layouts
section_2_comparison_baseline.why_this_is_the_right_comparison: This represents the standard approach of integrating new storage technologies by abstracting them as traditional disks and using existing data layouts (NSM, PAX) on top of that abstraction.
section_2_comparison_baseline.limiting_design_assumption: MEMS-based storage should be abstracted as a one-dimensional, disk-like device, where data is accessed in coarse-grained units like logical blocks or pages. This hides the two-dimensional physical properties of the device.
pointers: [p. 3, quote: '...mapping MEMS-based storage devices into disk-like devices.']
[p. 4, quote: '...both NSM or PAX bring values of all attributes in a page into the memory.']

section_3_primary_mechanism_tooling_clas.what_is_being_optimized: The physical placement of relational attributes and records onto the 2D grid of MEMS tip sectors.
section_3_primary_mechanism_tooling_clas.state_or_ir: The physical data layout on the MEMS media sled.
section_3_primary_mechanism_tooling_clas.output: A data layout that enables selective retrieval of attribute subsets (columns) by aligning them for parallel access by MEMS tips.

section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.summary: Introduces a 2D-aware data layout (FRM) that stripes records across MEMS tip regions to vertically align attributes, enabling efficient columnar access.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.baseline_assumption: Data should be laid out in 1D pages or blocks, either record by record (NSM) or with all attributes for a few records grouped in a page (PAX).
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.why_baseline_did_not_include_it: The baseline aimed for compatibility with existing systems by abstracting the MEMS device as a disk, which hides the 2D physical structure necessary for such a layout.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.mechanism_level_implementation: A relation is striped across tip regions. Each attribute of a record occupies an integer number of consecutive tip sectors. Subsequent records are placed in the same row of tip regions, aligning attributes across records at the same x-coordinates. This pattern is repeated for subsequent rows of tip regions.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.tradeoffs_or_costs: The layout is more complex than page-based schemes. Cache performance can be worse than PAX in specific low-selectivity, high-projectivity query scenarios.

section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.summary: Changes the data access granularity from coarse logical blocks to fine-grained tip sectors, allowing the system to retrieve only the attributes required by a query.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.baseline_assumption: Data is read from storage in fixed-size units like pages or logical blocks (e.g., 512 bytes), which forces retrieval of all attributes within that block.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.why_baseline_did_not_include_it: The disk-like abstraction used by the baseline mandates a block-based I/O interface for compatibility with existing operating systems and database engines.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.mechanism_level_implementation: The data retrieval algorithm activates only the MEMS tips corresponding to the attributes needed for a query. It calculates the number of access passes required based on the number of needed tips versus the hardware limit on concurrently active tips.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.tradeoffs_or_costs: Requires a custom data retrieval logic that is tightly coupled with the hardware characteristics and the FRM layout, breaking the standard block device abstraction.
pointers: [p. 4, quote: 'data in a complete disk page or a logical block has to be retrieved together.']

principles.name: Hardware-Aware
principles.mechanism_trigger: The FRM layout algorithm explicitly models the 2D grid of tip regions, the size of tip sectors, and the seek time characteristics (preferring Y-movement over X-movement).
principles.why_it_applies: The entire data placement strategy is designed to directly exploit the physical, two-dimensional architecture of the MEMS device, rather than layering on top of a generic block abstraction.
principles.pointer: [p. 6, quote: 'we will consider the physical movement property of MEMS-based storage... we should first consider a new row which has the same x coordinate, and y coordinate offset by one...']

principles.name: Abstraction Lifting
principles.mechanism_trigger: The system rejects the baseline's disk-like abstraction of MEMS storage.
principles.why_it_applies: The paper's central argument is that the 1D disk abstraction is harmful ('MEMS-based storage devices lose their two-dimensional property' [p. 3]). FRM lifts this abstraction to expose the underlying 2D grid and tip-level addressability to the data placement layer to gain performance.
principles.pointer: [p. 4, quote: 'by treating MEMS-based storage as two-dimensional storage for placing relational data, the gap between the main memory and secondary storage can be reduced notably.']

principles.name: Result-Preserving Work Avoidance
principles.mechanism_trigger: The retrieval mechanism activates only the tips corresponding to attributes present in the query's projection list.
principles.why_it_applies: The system avoids the I/O work of reading attributes not required by the query. This skipped work does not change the final query result, as the unused attributes are irrelevant to the computation.
principles.pointer: [p. 4, quote: 'I/O time is wasted retrieving unnecessary attributes by mapping MEMS-based storage to one-dimensional devices.']

principles.name: Hardware-Aware
principles.mechanism_trigger: The retrieval algorithm explicitly checks if the number of tips needed for the required attributes exceeds the maximum number of concurrently active tips allowed by the hardware.
principles.why_it_applies: The retrieval plan (number of passes) is directly determined by a physical hardware constraint (maximum active tips), demonstrating hardware awareness.
principles.pointer: [p. 7, quote: 'if Na is larger than the maximum number of concurrent tips, then the number of retrievals... is equal to ⌈ Na / the number of maximum concurrent tips ⌉.']

rejected_or_borderline_principles.name: Bottleneck-Oriented
rejected_or_borderline_principles.reason_rejected_or_borderline: While the paper identifies the I/O gap as a bottleneck, Wv is a more specific principle that describes the mechanism (avoiding I/O for unneeded data) rather than just the motivation.

section_7_compound_equation.equation: Disk-like Abstraction + Al + Ha + Wv -> FRM

principle_composition_rationale.why_these_principles_work_together: The system's performance gain comes from lifting the simplifying disk abstraction (Al) to create a hardware-aware (Ha) data layout. This new layout, in turn, enables a retrieval strategy that avoids result-irrelevant I/O work (Wv) by fetching only the necessary data columns at a fine granularity.

what_each_principle_contributes.contribution_to_equation: Provides the physical constraints and opportunities (2D grid, concurrent tips, seek costs) that the new data layout and retrieval algorithms are designed to exploit.
Enables the design by rejecting the performance-limiting 1D block device abstraction and exposing the true hardware structure to the database.
Explains the primary performance benefit: the hardware-aware layout allows the system to provably skip reading unnecessary attributes without affecting query correctness.

principle_composition_rationale.transfer_question: In what other domains could lifting a simplifying hardware abstraction enable a new data layout that avoids unnecessary work by matching access granularity to hardware capabilities?

section_8_physical_properties_summary.concrete_number: Can be >2x better than NSM, but can be worse than PAX in low selectivity/high projectivity cases.

best_candidate_new_principle.name: Granularity Rewriting
best_candidate_new_principle.definition: Restructuring a system's unit of work, storage, or consistency to a finer or coarser grain to better match workload demands or hardware capabilities.
best_candidate_new_principle.mechanism_pattern: The system moves from a coarse-grained unit of storage and access (the logical block) to a fine-grained one (the tip sector). This change in granularity is the enabling mechanism for avoiding work.
best_candidate_new_principle.why_existing_principles_are_insufficient: Ha explains the motivation (hardware has fine-grained tips), Al explains the prerequisite (breaking the block abstraction), and Wv explains the benefit (skipping I/O). None of them capture the core design action of changing the fundamental unit of data management from a block to a tip sector.
best_candidate_new_principle.reusability_beyond_this_paper: This pattern is common. Examples include moving from table-level locks to row-level locks, from monolithic RPCs to fine-grained microservices, or from coarse-grained cache lines to sub-block tracking. It represents a general strategy for improving efficiency and parallelism.
best_candidate_new_principle.pointer: [p. 7, quote: 'data can be accessed by tip sectors instead of logical blocks']

section_11_normalized_summary.one_sentence_mechanism: FRM exploits the 2D physical structure of MEMS storage by striping relational data at the fine granularity of individual tip sectors, enabling hardware-aware retrieval of only the columns required by a query to avoid unnecessary I/O.
